headline: Gusts hit 87 km/h by this evening, so the brick moves to tomorrow at 07:00 and today goes in the pool.
body:
You are right about the wind, and it is worse than it feels: **gusts 71 km/h by midday, 87 by 19:00**, south-easter all day. That is not hard riding, it is a crosswind taking your front wheel. Tomorrow morning is **8-10 km/h with gusts under 33** and 14-21 degrees - close to perfect. Roll out at 07:00; by 15:00 it is 28 degrees.

Today: **1,800 m in the pool** - 400 warm-up, 6 x 150 off 20 s, 400 easy - and the full ankle block. Zero ankle load, legs fresh for tomorrow.

Tomorrow: **85 km at 140-150 bpm**, 155 cap on the climbs, then **20 minutes off the bike** at 6:45-7:00/km. I have cut that from 35. The transition is the test; the extra 15 minutes only buy risk on an ankle that got worse after Thursday's run.

This morning's numbers still say go - **HRV 64 against a 14-day mean of 60**, first above-baseline morning since 31 August. The wind is the only reason today changed.

That ankle needs a physio on Monday. Fifteen days out, it is the only thing here that ends your race.
